stories.headline: 'No impact on India-US ties': Tharoor says Trump retains power on tariffs, Iran war
stories.title: 'No impact on India-US ties': Tharoor says Trump retains power on tariffs, Iran war
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: NEW DELHI: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor on Friday said the results of the US midterm elections would have little impact on India-US relations, asserting that President Donald Trump retains considerable powers to pursue his foreign policy agenda despite the ruling party's electoral setback.

Speaking in Thiruvananthapuram, Tharoor said the US election results would not change Washington's approach towards key issues such as tariffs, sanctions on countries buying Russian oil, the Iran war or the Ukraine conflict." Whether it comes to tariffs, whether it comes to sanctions for buying Russian oil, whether it comes to the Iran war itself, whether it comes to any initiative he takes on the Ukraine war.
All of this, he's completely unaffected by the election result," Tharoor said.

He explained that while Congress has significant powers over budgetary matters and can restrict or approve government spending, the President enjoys considerable discretion in foreign policy and international affairs.
Tharoor said that even when it comes to military action, the President can proceed without seeking approval for an initial period of up to 60 days.
However, Congress can exercise its financial powers to restrict expenditure, particularly in the case of an expensive military campaign.
"Those in India who are expecting this to have some impact on our relationship with the US, I think, are completely mistaken," he said.

Commenting on the election outcome, Tharoor described it as an extraordinary setback for the ruling party, pointing out that midterm elections traditionally serve as a course correction for the party in power.
He also highlighted the gains made by candidates from minority communities and people of Indian origin, including the election of a mayor of Indian origin in Los Angeles.
Tharoor said the results reflected the vibrancy of American democracy but maintained that the outcome would not significantly alter Trump's ability to take decisions on international affairs.
Priyanka Jaiswal has four years of experience in digital journalism, news agency reporting and video production.
Currently with The Times of India, she covers public policy, politics and global affairs.

stories.headline: Democrats vow to end Iran war as US midterm defeat hits Trump; oil prices fall
stories.title: Democrats vow to end Iran war as US midterm defeat hits Trump; oil prices fall
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 5: The Democrats have vowed to make ending the Iran war a priority after their sweeping victory in the US midterm elections, dealing a major political setback to President Donald Trump and his Republican Party, reports BBC. Democratic Senate leader Chuck Schumer said ending the conflict would be a priority, adding that cutting off funding to the Department of Defence could be considered if it was the only way to secure a swift end to the war. Hakeem Jeffries, the Democratic leader in the House of Representatives and likely to become the next Speaker, said his party would hold the Trump administration accountable and act as a check on what he described as an “out-of-control executive branch”. “We don’t work for Donald Trump. We don’t work for JD Vance. We don’t work for the Supreme Court. We work for the American people,” he said, according to the BBC. Jeffries also accused what he called the “Trump Cartel” of massive corruption, promising to hold those responsible accountable. The election outcome has also triggered a sharp fall in global oil prices, with crude touching its lowest level in two months amid expectations of renewed diplomatic engagement between the US and Iran. However, analysts feel that expectations might be premature, given the difficulties in negotiations between Washington and Tehran. Iran, he said, would seek “a top price” for fully reopening the Strait of Hormuz and allowing commercial shipping to move freely. The conflict had effectively closed the strategic waterway, through which around 20 per cent of the world’s oil and liquefied natural gas normally passes, triggering a surge in global energy prices. Trump acknowledged that the Iran war was largely responsible for his party’s electoral defeat, while Vice-President JD Vance also said the conflict had contributed to the Republican setback. Russia, meanwhile, said the Democratic victory would not alter Washington’s foreign policy towards Ukraine. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Moscow would continue pursuing its interests either militarily or through negotiations. China has called for a “constructive, strategically stable China-US relationship” ahead of a planned meeting between Trump and President Xi Jinping this month. Beijing is expected to push for a trade agreement, with questions also emerging over whether Taiwan could figure in the negotiations. The Democratic victory has also raised questions about divisions within the party, particularly over Israel policy, which could complicate its efforts to shape the administration’s foreign and domestic agenda.

stories.title: Ghaziabad woman wins election in US
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Her electoral success is particularly interesting given her journey across different fields.
Before entering politics, Haider studied wildlife sciences in India, moved to the US after marriage, and built a career as a certified yoga instructor.
She gradually became involved in community initiatives before making her mark in local politics.
Saba Haider grew up in Ghaziabad, where her father, Syed Ali Haider, worked as an engineer before retiring.
Her mother, Chandni, recalls to TOI that her daughter was interested in public affairs from an early age.
School debates and speaking competitions were among the activities that helped shape her confidence.
According to her mother, Haider's academic interests and willingness to participate in public discussions eventually influenced her interest in politics.
She completed her schooling at Holy Child School in Ghaziabad.
She then enrolled at Ram Chameli Chadha Vishvas Girls' College, where she pursued a Bachelor of Science degree.
Her academic journey subsequently took her to Aligarh Muslim University.
There, she specialised in wildlife sciences and earned a gold medal, an achievement that marked an important milestone before her move to the US.
Haider married Ali Kazmi, a computer science engineer whose family belongs to Bulandshahr district in Uttar Pradesh, in 2006.

stories.headline: Congress-BJP slug it out over a milk federation election result in Maharashtra
stories.title: Congress-BJP slug it out over a milk federation election result in Maharashtra
stories.summary: In Maharashtra, the fallout from the Gokul Milk Federation election intensified on November 5 as Congress accused the BJP of stealing milk producers’ votes after Satej Patil’s panel clinched 13 of 25 seats
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Developments in the aftermath of Maharashtra’s largest milk federation election have churned Maharashtra politics.
On Thursday (November 5), Rahul Gandhi accused the Bharatiya Janata Party of stealing milk producers’ votes.
This was days after Congress leader Satej Patil’s panel won a wafer-thin majority against the Mahayuti panel by gaining 13 of the 25 seats in the Gokul Milk Federation election.

Now, ahead of the chairperson’s election, which is to be held on November 10, the Maharashtra cabinet has approved a controversial amendment that allows the State government to appoint five nominated directors (four of whom will have voting rights) to large cooperatives with turnovers exceeding ₹500 crore.
This is likely to tilt the majority in favour of the Mahayuti, which had earned 12 seats.
Congress will now take out a protest march in Kolhapur on November 9 against the State government's decision to nominate directors.
“This is nothing but murder of democracy.
This is the disrespect of the farmers’ voice,” Satej Bunty Patil said.
He said the party will fight this battle in the court as well as on the streets.
The Congress leader has already moved the Bombay High Court in the matter.
Gokul, or Kolhapur District Cooperative Milk Producers’ Union, is one of the most fiercely contested cooperative battles.
Gokul was founded in 1963.

stories.headline: A man named Chris will be New Zealand's next prime minister, whichever party wins the election
stories.title: A man named Chris will be New Zealand's next prime minister, whichever party wins the election
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Wellington (AP) New Zealand is choosing a new government in a national election that concludes Saturday.
But one outcome is already known: The next prime minister will be a man named Chris.
The leaders of the nation's two biggest political parties bear that name.
Center-right National is helmed by Christopher Luxon, who has been prime minister since the 2023 election, when his party ousted center-left Labour, led by Chris Hipkins.
Both leaders in the "battle of the Chrises" are, according to most opinion polls, fairly unpopular with voters.

The ascension of political Chrises is linked to the popularity of the name Christopher for New Zealand children until the mid-1980s, peaking in 1968 when nearly 800 babies were given the name, according to government data.
In 2025, just 20 newborns were named Christopher.
Here's how to tell the political leaders apart.
The National party's leader and incumbent prime minister, Luxon, 56, was one of more than 600 Christophers born in New Zealand in 1970.
When he took power after the 2023 election, Luxon was a relative political novice who had first been elected to Parliament in 2020.
Before entering politics he was head of national carrier Air New Zealand.
He also worked in the United States and Canada as an executive for consumer packaged goods firm Unilever.

stories.headline: Only 1 local terrorist active, Srinagar faces persistent threat inputs: IGP Kashmir
stories.title: Only 1 local terrorist active, Srinagar faces persistent threat inputs: IGP Kashmir
stories.summary: Srinagar, Nov 5: Inspector General of Police (IGP), Kashmir Zone, Sujit Kumar said on Thursday that only one local terrorist remains active in the Valley, even as Srinagar continues to receive persistent threat inputs that have prompted additional security measures. Addressing a news conference, the IGP Kashmir identified the lone active local terrorist as Muhammed Lateef Bhat of Kulgam, who is linked to two terror attacks earlier this year - one in Anantnag that killed a police official and another in Kulgam in which two migrant workers from Chhattisgarh were shot dead. “There is certainly one local terrorist, supported by a few foreign terrorists. We have some footprints, but giving a fixed number of active terrorists would be an exaggeration because they are constantly moving from one place to another,” Kumar said. He said that there is no official data available on any infiltration this year. Kumar said security forces continue to track the group based on available inputs. Referring to recent encounters in Budgam, the IGP said the terrorists killed in two operations were shot dead in the upper reaches. The area connects with the Pir Panjal range and Kishtwar, terrain that has remained a focus of joint operations by the Army, J&K Police, and Central Armed Police Forces. Sustained domination of these high-altitude areas has enabled successful operations, he noted. On the technological capabilities of the terrorists, IGP Kashmir said said the gadgets they are using are under surveillance. “Whatever technology they are using is on our radar. We have devised a mechanism and will not allow their nefarious designs to succeed,” he said, while declining to share operational specifics. The IGP Kashmir also detailed security arrangements along the National Highway. He said that following a terror attack, a security mechanism was put in place and aligned along the highway. "Further realignment will be discussion with other agencies," Kumar said. “In Srinagar we get inputs, which is why extra measures have been put in place. Still, we recover IEDs around the National Highway - threats are there,” he said. About restrictions, the IGP Kashmir said that the matter would have to be discussed with other agencies. The remarks come amid ongoing implementation of the winter security strategy. Earlier this week, Kumar reviewed the Srinagar City security grid and arrangements along the Jhelum corridor, directing officers to strengthen coordination and operational preparedness. Police officials said the security grid remains focused on intelligence-based operations, area domination and inter-agency synergy to neutralise residual threats and protect public spaces, including key routes.

stories.title: Turkish lawmakers approve defence pact with Pakistan, Saudi Arabia
stories.summary: Turkish legislators on Thursday ratified a defense cooperation agreement among Turkey, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia as Riyadh seeks increased regional support in its conflict with Iran-backed Houthi rebels in neighboring Yemen. The vote also came as countries in the region remain anxious about the prospects of a new escalation in the US-Iran war, which would likely spill over into neighboring countries. During previous rounds of fighting, Iran has lashed out at US-allied Gulf Arab countries, including Saudi Arabia. The 16-article Mecca Joint Defense Agreement, signed in August, commits the three countries to regard an attack against one as an attack on all three, to work together to deter threats and deepen military cooperation, share intelligence and strengthen defense industry ties. stories.headline: DRDO successfully tests quasi-ballistic missile Pralay
stories.title: DRDO successfully tests quasi-ballistic missile Pralay
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 5: The Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) on Thursday successfully flight-tested the indigenously developed quasi-ballistic missile ‘Pralay’ from Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island off the Odisha coast. The test was conducted at around 11.10 am as part of user evaluation trials, with all objectives successfully met, as confirmed by data from range instruments deployed by the Integrated Test Range, Chandipur. Developed by DRDO’s Research Centre Imarat, Hyderabad, along with other laboratories, the missile has been produced by Bharat Dynamics Limited. With the successful test, its induction into the armed forces has become imminent. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh congratulated DRDO, the armed forces and industry partners, saying the missile’s advanced technologies would further strengthen the military’s technological capabilities and operational preparedness against emerging threats.

article_sentences: A bench of Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice Manmohan quashed the proceedings, allowing the appeal against the Bombay High Court's order by which it had refused to quash it.
The deceased was a Class 7 student aged 12 who met with an accident within the school premises when a pillar under construction collapsed and fell on her, resulting in severe fatal injuries.
The incident happened on February 15, 2020 in a school in Amaravati District.

A case was subsequently filed by the deceased girl's father alleging that the school's director and the hostel superintendent deliberately made the kaccha and standardless construction of the pillar and did not take the precautions while constructing the pillar.
The appellants were thereafter prosecuted under Section 304 read with Section 34 of the IPC (now Section 105 and Section 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023/BNS respectively).
The appellants approached the High Court seeking quashing of the case against them.

However, the High Court refused to quash the proceedings, relying on a Chemical Analyser's report, which showed that the cement-sand-aggregate ratio in the mortar was not maintained, and on the spot panchnama, which said the pillar had no solid base.

It further held that there was a breach of duty and that “though there was no intention to cause death but admittedly knowledge was there that sub standard material while constructing the base for installation of pillar may cause harm or death to the person.”
Aggrieved by the High Court's refusal, the appellants approached the Supreme Court.
Before the Supreme Court, the appellants argued that no voluntary commission of an offence was made out in the prosecution's case, therefore, Section 304 of the IPC would not apply.
It was also submitted that Section 304A of the IPC would also not apply because the appellants' lack of care could be one of the causes of death, but not the direct consequence.
For context, Section 304 of the IPC deals with the offence of culpable homicide not amounting to murder, and Section 304A deals with the offence of death caused by negligent act.

stories.headline: Madhya Pradesh cabinet approves ₹63,296 crore plan for five greenfield corridors
stories.title: Madhya Pradesh cabinet approves ₹63,296 crore plan for five greenfield corridors
stories.summary: MP is developing a modern road network through the construction of state highways, four-lane, six-lane and eight-lane roads, as well as greenfield expressways: CM Mohan Yadav
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'cabinet approves' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Madhya Pradesh government is moving ahead with a plan to build five greenfield expressway corridors across the state at an estimated cost of ₹63,296 crore.
The decision was reviewed at the 49th board meeting of the Madhya Pradesh Road Development Corporation (MPRDC), chaired by Chief Minister Dr. Mohan Yadav on Thursday.
The proposed four-lane, access-controlled corridors will span a total length of 1,398 km.
They include Bhopal–Mandsaur (258 km), Sagar–Satna (227 km), Jabalpur–Ashapur (358 km), Bhopal–Gwalior (320 km) and Katni–Singrauli (235 km).
Feasibility reports for the first three corridors are being prepared, with consultants submitting alignment options for review.
For the Bhopal–Gwalior and Katni–Singrauli routes, the tender process for selecting DPR consultants is underway.
CM Yadav directed officials to expedite ongoing road projects and stressed that no village, town or city should remain deprived of all-weather road connectivity.
He also renamed the corporation’s proposed Highway Fund as the ‘Viksit Madhya Pradesh Sankalp Path’.

The board approved several key decisions, including 100% divestment of equity in the four-lane Jaora–Nayagaon BOT project, creation of new senior posts, acquisition of the PAM Building in Bhopal, and exemption of combine harvesters from toll charges at all MPRDC-operated plazas.

stories.headline: Dissident NC MLAs close ranks, hold 4th meeting since cabinet expansion
stories.title: Dissident NC MLAs close ranks, hold 4th meeting since cabinet expansion
stories.summary: Srinagar, Nov 5: The internal crisis in the ruling National Conference (NC) appears to be moving towards a possible negotiated settlement, with a group of disgruntled legislators scheduled to meet party president Farooq Abdullah and Chief Minister Omar Abdullah to formally present their grievances and demands. The Friday's meeting could provide an opportunity to address the growing discontent within the party following the recent cabinet expansion. Talking to Greater Kashmir, MLA Hazratbal, Salman Ali Sagar said that there has been a full reach out from the party to these legislators. "There were some prior engagements and Chief Minister (Omar Abdullah) Sahab had some personal engagements after the cabinet expansion," he said. "Some party leaders were also busy after the cabinet expansion as a result of which things got dragged for a few days." However, he said that during the last five to six days, the party had been in touch with all these legislators. Salman said that none of these NC leaders were rebellious against the party. "They say they have certain issues and grievances and want the party leadership to redress those grievances," he said. Salman said that he had personally met MLA Gurez, Nazir Ahmad Khan (Gurezi), and MLA Lolab, Qaysar Jamshaid Lone, on Thursday and around four more prominent MLAs. "I also talked to MLA Gulmarg, Pirzada Farooq Ahmed Shah, and MLA Budhal, Javed Iqbal Choudhary," he said. "By and large, all of them have demanded redressal of their grievances, nothing more." Salman said that these legislators will call on NC President Farooq Abdullah at his residence on Friday. "They can also meet Chief Minister Omar (Abdullah) Sahab if he does not have prior official engagements. "Everything will hopefully be sorted out after the meeting with Farooq (Abdullah) Sahab and they will come out with a positive mindset," he said. "Whatever is doable will be done." Meanwhile, according to sources, the dissident NC legislators continued their consultations late Thursday evening at the Srinagar residence of MLA Pampore, Hasnain Masoodi, to finalise their strategy ahead of the meeting with the party leadership. The sources said that 20 dissident NC MLAs participated in the meeting including 16 physically and four virtually. An NC MLA, who participated in the meeting, said that the dissident NC legislators had been asked by the NC President Farooq Abdullah and Chief Minister Omar Abdullah to meet them at the residence of Farooq Abdullah on Friday. He said that the meeting held on Thursday evening had decided that a delegation representing the group would meet the party high command and put forth their grievances and demands. It was their fourth meeting since cabinet expansion. On Wednesday evening, around a dozen NC dissident legislators assembled at the Haiderpora, Srinagar residence of MLA Gulmarg, Pirzada Farooq Ahmad Shah, after another meeting earlier in the day at the Tulsi Bagh, Srinagar residence of MLA Gurez, Nazir Ahmad Khan (Gurezi). The consultations have gathered momentum since the dissident group of NC legislators first assembled at the Humhama residence of Qaysar Jamshaid Lone last week. Seventeen NC legislators and an independent MLA from Thanamandi reportedly took an oath of collective solidarity at the meeting, pledging to pursue their concerns jointly rather than take individual positions. The group included MLA Pampore Hasnain Masoodi, MLA Rajpora Ghulam Mohiuddin Mir, MLA Karnah Javid Ahmad, MLA Khan Sahab Saifuddin Bhat, MLA Tangmarg Pirzada Farooq Ahmad Shah, MLA Eidgah Mubarik Gul, MLA Gurez Nazir Ahmad Khan (Gurezi), MLA Sonawari Hilal Akbar Lone, MLA Bijbehara Bashir Ahmad Shah (Veeri), MLA Anantnag West Abdul Majid Bhat (Larmi), MLA Poonch Haveli Aijaz Ahmad Jan, MLA Budhal Javid Iqbal Choudhary, MLA Ramban Arjun Singh Raju, MLA Gulabgarh Khursheed Ahmad, MLA Uri Sajad Shafi, and independent MLA from Thanamandi Muzaffar Iqbal Khan. Inside sources in NC said that around two dozen legislators are dissatisfied, although the number of those who have formally joined the collective initiative is lower. They said the dissident NC legislators had prepared a charter of demands covering governance and organisational matters. These include stepping up efforts for the restoration of statehood and special status for Jammu and Kashmir, implementing the Dachigam resolution on cabinet restructuring and ministerial accountability, and replacing the Chief Minister’s inner circle. They have also sought the formation of a consultative advisory group comprising two to three legislators to regularly brief the CM on governance issues and the implementation of developmental works. On the organisational front, their demands include setting up a high-powered disciplinary committee and an inquiry panel to address grievances, strengthening the party’s media and communication cell, holding regular meetings of the NC Working Committee, establishing an election cell, and undertaking comprehensive organisational restructuring. Meanwhile, efforts appear to have been made to prevent the differences from escalating into an open confrontation, particularly over the position of senior leader and six-time MLA from Eidgah, Mubarik Gul. Two NC legislators visited Gul at his residence on Wednesday and reportedly persuaded him not to take any unilateral decision ahead of the proposed meeting with the party leadership. Gul had planned to address a news conference to explain his grievances over his exclusion from the recent cabinet expansion but subsequently deferred it following the death of senior party leader Sheikh Ghulam Qadir (Pardesi) and father of NC MLA Lal Chowk, Ahsan Pardesi. Meanwhile, Gul’s son, Younus Gul, defended his father’s position, saying that seeking legitimate rights after decades of service to the party could not be construed as rebellion. Speaking to reporters, Younus said his father had been associated with the NC for 40 to 50 years and had won several elections while remaining loyal to the party. “Asking for your right is not rebellion. If someone comes from outside and demands something, that may be different. But a person who has served the party for 40-50 years and won seven elections cannot be treated this way,” he said. Younus also urged the party leadership to identify those working against the organisation’s interests rather than treating the assertion of legitimate demands by senior leaders as an act of indiscipline. The discontent has been particularly pronounced since the October 27 cabinet expansion, during which four new ministers were inducted, taking the Council of Ministers (CoM) to its maximum permissible strength of nine. Gul, a six-time legislator and former Speaker of the Legislative Assembly, was among the prominent leaders left out. Uncertainty over his organisational position further complicated the situation. Although NC President Farooq Abdullah appointed Gul as General Secretary on October 27, a subsequent order issued on October 30 directed Ali Mohammad Sagar, who had joined the cabinet, to continue holding the post until further orders. Earlier, senior NC legislator Majid Larmi had disclosed that Gul’s elevation as General Secretary was proposed during the meeting of legislators at Qaysar Jamshaid Lone’s residence. Gul had reportedly indicated that he would take up the responsibility after first pacifying his supporters. The latest consultations suggest that the dissident legislators are seeking a collective accommodation within the party rather than an immediate confrontation with its leadership. Meanwhile, former legislator Choudhary Akram has denied reports that he was planning to resign from the party, asserting that he remained with the NC and continued to support Chief Minister Omar Abdullah. The NC leadership has officially played down reports of internal rebellion, describing the legislators’ earlier gathering at the Srinagar residence of MLA Lolab Qaysar Jamshaid Lone as a routine social interaction ahead of the Darbar Move. However, the continued consultations, the proposed charter of demands, and Friday’s expected meeting indicate that the party leadership faces a substantive set of organisational and governance concerns that will need to be addressed. The party is under scrutiny particularly after the resignation of senior party leader and Member of Parliament from Srinagar-Budgam parliamentary constituency, Aga Syed Ruhullah, who parted ways with NC after 24 years.
